name: Central banks vs energy inflation
backstory: The Iran war cut oil supply and pushed up [[headline inflation]], so central banks have been trying to decide whether the price jump fades on its own or leaks into wages and services. Euro area inflation reached 4%, the Bank of England hiked to 4%, and the Fed sits at 3.875%.
today: The PCE price index rose 3.8% from a year earlier in October, matching forecasts, and third quarter [[GDP]] was revised up to 4.3%, so the economy is strong while prices are hot. That leaves the Fed's rate barely above inflation, and a CNBC commentary argues that Kevin Warsh should hike instead of betting on a productivity boom the way Greenspan did. The ECB's account of its October meeting adds that energy prices pushed oil and gas above its own adverse scenario, and markets at one point priced in more than four extra hikes before settling on just under three. Households are feeling it too, with even toys getting pricier and holiday budgets shrinking.

name: Iran war and oil
backstory: The conflict began in early 2026 and cut global oil output by 12 million barrels a day in March, but prices stayed below records because stored oil filled the gap. The IEA says the Hormuz shock lifted the world's oil and gas import bill 25% to $1.6 trillion, and pump prices recently fell to their lowest level since March.
today: WTI crude rose 1.99% to 83.68, its second straight gain, because tension in the Middle East outweighed expectations for a global supply surplus. The ECB's account of its October meeting says freight rates from the Gulf to Europe hit record highs, diesel [[crack spreads]] sit above the levels after Russia's 2022 invasion, and the odds of a US-Iran peace deal by the end of 2026 were the lowest since the war began. Meanwhile the UAE says it expects 7% to 8% growth next year as the IMF lifts its forecast, which shows that the Gulf is coping better than the headlines might suggest.

name: AI trade jitters
backstory: The biggest AI-linked tech firms hold up so much of the S&P 500 that doubts about AI hit the whole market. Nvidia's CEO left on Nov 12, a selloff followed, official papers warned that AI [[valuation]]s look stretched, and the index fell four straight weeks. Then Nvidia's board approved Huang's return and the Nasdaq jumped 6.51% on Monday.
today: Nvidia gave back a big chunk of Monday's rally, and according to Vanda Research the gains of retail investors who bought the dip last week are now nearly all gone. Oracle and CoreWeave sank early and then bounced, so the day ended less ugly than it began. Vance said he was assured Huang was not under a DOJ investigation, while a CNBC column says Treasury Secretary Bessent's about-face on Huang shows how unsettled the administration's stance on Nvidia and China is. The ECB's account of its October meeting also lists worries about the increasingly debt-financed AI investment cycle.

name: US midterms and the dollar
backstory: The midterms produced what headlines call a Democratic rout, and markets asked how divided government might change tariffs, spending and the dollar. The dollar then had its biggest rally since 2024, with headlines crediting hawkish Fed bets and not the election, and it hit a 20-month high, its strongest since March 2025.
today: The dollar index slipped 0.13% to 103.67 as Treasury yields fell, and commentary now suggests the dollar may be peaking. The US also announced plans for new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including China and the EU, and the Swiss franc gained as a safe haven. Tuesday's consumer confidence reading jumped to 103.3 after the Democratic wins, though inflation worries persist.

name: Yen defense
backstory: A weak yen pushed Japan to intervene [sell dollars to buy yen] in the currency market, including a record $50 billion in one day. The BOJ's 1.25% rate is 2.625 percentage points below the Fed's 3.875%, which encourages selling yen to hold dollars. Japan's economy unexpectedly shrank in Q3 as energy costs bit.
today: USD/JPY was 159.32, down 0.04%, so the yen was little changed. The BOJ chief played down soft consumption data and signaled a near-term rate hike. Japan's inflation accelerated, and the country posted a sixth straight monthly trade deficit. A Reuters-style analysis says BOJ ambiguity on the path of hikes could tempt yen bears. In Friday's Asian session, the Nikkei fell 2.9% on chip and metals stocks.
